courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Managing Business Data in Excel and Tableau
courses.description: This course will introduce fundamental business data management skills and business intelligence tools that are essential for business management. The course will help students to develop basic concepts of data collection and handling, and to know how to structure and solve business problems using Microsoft Excel and Tableau, the most popular and penetrated tool, with the support of Office 365 for Cloud-based communication. Topics such as Storytelling with Tableau, SharePoint, Formulas and Functions, Charts, Subtotals, PivotTables, PivotCharts, What-If Analysis, Specialized Functions, Statistical Functions, Multiple-Sheet Workbook Management, XML, Power Add-Ins, Workbook Distribution, Templates, Styles, and Macros will be covered.
courses.learning_outcomes:
• To learn the essential operations using Cloud computing through course’s SharePoint Site and Excel
• To develop basic concepts of data collection and data handling
• To learn how to structure and solve business problems using Microsoft Excel
• To develop skills in critical thinking through Discussion Forum of course’s SharePoint Site
• To apply skills to monitor daily business activities using Excel and Tableau through designated course assignments
courses.course_syllabus:
• Course Introduction
• Introduction to Excel Creating and Formatting a Worksheet
• Introduction to SharePoint Site
• Introduction to Tableau Prep + Tableau Desktop
• Formulas and Functions Performing Quantitative Analysis
• Charts Depicting Data Visually
• Datasets and Tables Managing Large Volumes of Data
• Subtotals, PivotTables, and PivotCharts Summarizing and Analyzing Data
• What-If Analysis Using Decision-Making Tools
• Specialized Functions Using Date, Logical, Lookup, and Database
• Statistical Functions Analyzing Statistics
• Multiple-Sheet Workbook Management Ensuring Quality Control
• Imports, XML, and Power Add-Ins Managing Data
• Collaboration and Workbook Distribution Sharing Data with Others
• Templates, Styles, and Macros Standardizing Workbooks
• Exploring Excel data with Tableau, learn a drag-and-drop approach to visual analysis
• Creating Dashboards and Storytelling with Tableau
courses.feedback_evaluation: Mandatory Course and Teaching Evaluation (CTE) is conducted at the end of the course
courses.required_readings:
Shelly Cashman Series® Microsoft® Office 365 & Excel 2016: Comprehensive, Cengage.
Mary Anne Poatsy, Exploring Microsoft Office Excel 2016 Comprehensive, Pearson.

Tableau Free Training Videos: https://www.tableau.com/learn/training

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Business Economics
courses.description: This course intends to provide students with fundamentals to the understandings of both micro- and macro-economics for business decision makings and applications. Topics of microeconomics include demand and supply and elasticities, market structure and monopoly power, and the government and its economic functions. Topics of macroeconomics include unemployment, inflation, GDP and long term growth issues, aggregate supply and demand, and fiscal and monetary policies. Other topics of interests can also be included by the course instructor.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken DSME1030/DOTE1030, DSME1040/DOTE1040 and equivalent courses offered by other departments.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students should be able to understand, explain and apply:
(1) Basic concepts of scarcity, opportunity cost, demand and supply mechanisms, elasticity, and their applications to the business world.
(2) Different market structures such as perfect competition and monopoly.
(3) The concept of market failure and their remedies.
(4) Key macroeconomic variables such as gross domestic product (GDP), consumer price index (CPI), unemployment rate, and economic growth.
(5) The concepts of aggregate supply (AS), aggregate demand (AD), and the use of fiscal and monetary policies.
courses.course_syllabus: This course provides students with fundamentals to the understandings of both micro- and macro-economics for business decision makings and applications. Topics of Microeconomics include demand and supply and elasticities, market structure and monopoly power, and the government and its economic functions. Topics of Macroeconomics include unemployment, inflation, GDP and long term growth issues, aggregate supply and demand, and fiscal and monetary policies.

Topics and issues of current and emerging interest are discussed and explored. courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Corporate Economics
courses.description: This course provides economic views on the operations of enterprises in a market environment for corporate decision-making and strategy formulation. Students will learn how to analyse market structure and performance, how firms seek competitive advantage, and how industries change. Emphasis will be on the application of economic principles to major business decisions, including pricing, product mix, market entry, mergers, and adoption of new technologies. Industrial policy and its implications will also be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisites: (a) DSME1030/DOTE1030 and DSME1040/DOTE1040 and (b) HTMG1010 or MGNT1020
courses.learning_outcomes:
(1) Will be able to demonstrate understanding of what corporate strategies are
(2) Use economic theory to analyze issues in strategic management under different market structures
(3) Appreciate the importance of corporate strategic decisions
(4) Evaluate the role of game theoretic approaches to strategic choices
(5) Understand the challenges and opportunities of a firm under globalizations
courses.course_syllabus:
The overall aim of the course is to provide you with an understanding of strategic decisions in firms, and the contribution of economic principles to the analysis and formulation of corporate strategy. The course is linked to the theory of the firm, industrial organization and strategy research and application of game theory to corporate decisions making. In particular, we will emphasize on practical applications of topics from industrial economics and strategy to the real world. Finally, we will emphasize on the current macroeconomic and capital market environments to contemporary corporate decisions making.

Course Outline:
• Basic: Microeconomic Principles
• Economics of Scale and Scope
• Agency and Coordination
• The Vertical Boundaries of the firm
• Organizing Vertical Boundaries: Vertical
Integration and Its Alternatives
• Diversification
• Competitors and Competition
• Strategic Commitment
• The Dynamic of Pricing Rivalry
• Entry and Exit
• Industry Analysis
• Strategic Positioning for Competitive Advantage
• Current Topic in Corporate Economics
courses.feedback_evaluation: CTE and discussion with students outside classroom.
courses.required_readings: D. Besanko, D. Dranove, M. Shanley and S. Schaefer (BDSS), Economics of Strategy, John Wiley & Sons.
courses.recommended_readings:
Baye, Michael, Managerial Economics and Business Strategy, McGraw Hill.
Spulber, Daniel, Economics and Management of Competitive Strategy, World Scientific.

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Economic Aspects of Business Environment
courses.description: This course provides students with an economic perspective of the business environment and equips them with a solid grounding in business economics required for management studies at the university level. The major topics include: economic views of government and business; public choice and regulation; fiscal, monetary, trade and development policies; and the international environment. Examples will be drawn from Hong Kong, PRC in its economic reform since 1979 and the Asian NIE's competitive advantage and trade and industrial policy. Students are expected to exercise initiative in identifying aspects of special interest for in-depth reading. Empirical aspects of economic studies will be stressed through lecturing and case study.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisites: DSME1030/DOTE1030 and DSME1040/DOTE1040, or equivalent courses.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students would learn about (a) Hong Kong's banking system and its changes over the decade, (b) Hong Kong's currency board system, and (c) Hong Kong as an international financial centre, the last two with a comparative perspective.
courses.course_syllabus:
• Hong Kong's banking system in the first decades.
• Establishment of Hong Kong's monetary system.
• The current Hong Kong dollar link: operations, performance, and effects.
• The future of the Hong Kong dollar link.
• Hong Kong as an international financial centre.
courses.feedback_evaluation: CTE by the end of the term

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Game Theory for Business Strategy
courses.description: This course aims to develop a game theoretic framework for understanding strategies in business. When making managerial decisions, managers must take into account the reactions of rival firms, governments and their subordinates. Game theory offers a systematic way to analyze strategic decision-making process in business, including competition in oligopoly market, contract design, strategic use of information, auction and bargaining.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: DSME1030/DOTE1030
courses.course_syllabus:
• The Nature of Strategic Interaction
• Games with Sequential Moves
• Games with Simultaneous Moves
• Simultaneous-Move Games with Mixed Strategies
• Commitment and Strategic Moves: R&D and Price War
• Prisoners’Dilemma and Repetition: Choice of Product Mix
• Issues in Auctions
• Bargaining
courses.feedback_evaluation: Course and teaching evaluation
courses.required_readings: Dixit, Skeath, and Reiley, Games of Strategy, 3e, W. W. Norton & Company.
courses.recommended_readings:
Osborne, An introduction to game theory, Oxford University Press.
McMillan, Games, Strategies, and Managers, Oxford University Press.
Webster, Introduction to Game Theory in Business and Economics.
Gardner, Games for Business and Economics.

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Web Analytics
courses.description: The course focuses on the collection, analysis, and reporting of Internet data for purposes of optimizing web usage and enhancing business decisions. Both online and offline web analytics tools are used for measuring and analyzing web traffic, website performance, and visitor behavior in online commercial settings. Topics covered include web analytics concepts, web analytics technologies and techniques, visitor activity analysis methods, and web intelligence fundamentals.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite: DSME2011/DOTE2011 and DSME2021/DOTE2021 or permission of instructor.
courses.course_syllabus:
- Fundamentals of web analytics
- Big data and small data: different types of intelligence
- Website success measures: site goals, key performance indicators, and key metrics
- Tools and techniques of Web analytics: focus on learning the use of Google Analytics
- Website performance analysis: traffic analysis and search and keyword analysis
- Using visitor data to drive website improvement
- Leveraging digital analytics effectively
- Emerging analytics: social, mobile, and video

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Managerial Economics in the Information Age
courses.description: Managerial Economics combines economic theory and managerial practice, and it is the economic foundation of business analysis and strategy. This course focuses on the application of economic theories and tools to real world management problems and business challenges. Drawing on decision theory, game theory, models of markets and quantitative techniques, the course will apply fundamental concepts of economics to various business decisions, such as demand analysis, production and cost, pricing practices, capital budgeting and risk analysis. Particular attention will be paid to new industries in the information age.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisites: DSME1030/DOTE1030 and DSME1040/DOTE1040.
courses.course_syllabus:
• The fundamentals of managerial economics
• Market forces: demand and supply & quantitative demand analysis
• Managing firms in competitive, monopolistic, and monopolistically competitive market
• Game theory and oligopoly models
• Pricing strategies
• The economics of information
• Capital budgeting and investment under uncertainty
courses.feedback_evaluation: CTE by the end of the term

courses.recommended_readings:

courses.title: Information Systems Analysis and Design
courses.description: This course aims to introduce to students various activities associated with the development of business information systems. Students will learn to analyse information requirements and to design appropriate solutions that lead to sophisticated business systems. The concepts of system development life cycle (SDLC) and human- computer interaction will be introduced. Various methodologies, such as structured- and object-oriented analysis and design, will be emphasized. An introduction on how to use a CASE tool to help developing business information systems will also be given.

Topics covered include neural network, fuzzy logic, data mining and decision technologies relevant to financial services. Students will also learn to use Excel VBA to develop financial application systems.

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Global Logistics Management
courses.description: This course will examine the integrative role of logistics within the supply chain and look at logistics services from the perspective of logistic service providers. The general concepts and importance of global logistics management will be a major focus. We will provide students with an overall understanding of various activities handled by logistic service providers. Through problem-solving scenarios, projects and case studies, we will cover concepts, practical tools, and effective practices in logistics management. Topics include: introduction to the logistics functions and logistics industries, distribution strategies, warehousing and transportation management, design of the logistics networks, purchasing and outsourcing, and logistics information systems.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students should be able to:
(1) Understand the economic impacts of logistics
(2) Learn the importance of supply chain management
(3) Know the elements of logistics system
(4) Interact with logistics professionals or specialists using language used in logistics industry
(5) Develop skills and ability to solve logistics management problems.
courses.course_syllabus:
Review of Basic Concepts in Logistics
• Overview of Logistics
• Supply Chain Management
• Elements of Logistics Systems
courses.feedback_evaluation: CTE by end of the term

courses.recommended_readings:

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Global Supply Chain Management
courses.description: This course will examine the strategic role of supply chain management in global competition. We provide students with the concepts, decision models and practical tools necessary for effective decision-making in the various areas of supply chain. Through problem solving and case studies, the course will develop students’ intuition behind many key supply chain concepts and practices. We will demonstrate how cost reduction, productivity improvement, flexibility, speed, and customer satisfaction can be achieved through supply chain enhancement. Topics include: the strategic framework for supply chain management, planning the demand and supply in a supply chain, planning and managing inventories in a supply chain, information technology management and information sharing in a supply chain, strategic alliances and coordination.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students should be able to:
1. Understand the roles that supply chains play in a global economy. You will understand how supply chain work and contribute to the success of the firm.
2. Understand the goals and objectives of supply chain management. We will discuss key decisions and trade-offs involved in effectively managing supply chain.
3. Learn technical material on inventory theory, risk pooling, and optimization. This will also sharpen your general analytic and problem-solving skills.
4. Being able to address real business issues from the angle of inter-firm or inter-department relationships.
courses.course_syllabus: Particular topics include the understanding the supply chain, the strategic configuration of supply chains, distribution strategy, inventory management, instabilities caused by inadequate information-sharing, outsourcing, procurement (including e-markets), designing products for improved supply chain performance, strategic alliances, optimization approaches to strategic and tactical problems, the issues and opportunities brought by the Internet and the rise of e-business, and the many synergies between information technology and decision technology.
courses.feedback_evaluation: CTE by end of the term
courses.required_readings: Class handouts, including cases; extra write-ups; and slides.
courses.recommended_readings:
1. Simchi-Levi D, Kaminsky P., Simchi-Levi E., Designing & Managing the Supply Chain, concepts, strategies & case studies, McGraw-Hill Irwin.
2. Chopra S. Meindl P. Supply Chain Management, strategy, planning, and operations, Pearson Prentice Hall.

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Business Web Design and Authoring
courses.description: This course provides students with the basic knowledge required for designing and developing state-of-the-art interactive sites in the WWW. The primary focus will be on using Java Applets and JSP Web server pages to create Web business applications that can handle user requests and activate the relevant business processes. As the power of Web business applications relies heavily on access to the content of available databases, this course will also explore the technologies that have gained wide attention in the business information technology sectors, such as Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) and the Extensible Markup Language (XML). No prior programming knowledge is required.

After completing this course, students should be able to:
(1) understand the basic constructs in Java programming.
(2) identify the major features in Web design and user navigation.
(3) recognize the issues in interface design.
(4) understand the real-world Web applications from design to implementation.
(5) understand the basic rationale of the concepts in n-tier Web applications, both in client- and server-sides.

• Classes and Objects in Java

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Information Systems Practicum
courses.description: This course bridges the gap between classroom and real world. It requires students to complete a real-world information systems project, in collaboration with a company or organization. A minimum of three and a maximum of five students are required to form a project team, under the joint supervision of a MIS faculty member and a senior executive of the sponsoring company.

(1) work with IT/business professionals on real-world IT project
(2) understand the most current IT issues/management/trend in the commercial sector
(3) understand how real-world projects are managed and executed in a group setting
(4) improve their knowledge of real-world project development
(5) develop the skills (communication and leadership) required to complete IT projects

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Current and Regional Issues in Supply Chain and Logistics Management
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the current issues in supply chain and logistics management that are of special relevance to Hong Kong and mainland China. Hong Kong, a gateway (for Pearl River Delta) and a transshipment hub (for mainland China and other parts of Asia), houses many local and international logistics service providers. In this course, we examine the regional logistics industries that are of special relevance to Hong Kong and mainland China, as well as their principal agents. These agents include freight forwarders, warehousing operators, airlines, terminal operators, integrators, trucking operators, customs and electronic agents, etc. We will discuss the respective roles of these agents in the management of logistics within a supply chain. Recent trends in trade, distribution, and adoption of IT for cargo logistics are covered.
courses.learning_outcomes:
This course provides an overview of the current issues in supply chain and logistics management that are of special relevance to Hong Kong and mainland China. In this course, we examine the logistic infrastructure in the region, as well as the logistics industries and their principal agents. We first introduce the current developments in various transportation modes. We then will discuss the respective roles of the principal agents in the management of logistics within a supply chain. Recent trends in trade, distribution, and adoption of IT for cargo logistics are covered.
After completing this course, students should be able to:
1. Understand the current and regional issues in Supply Chain and Logistics Management and how they contribute to the success of the firm.
2. Understand the important of integration between Hong Kong and PRD.
3. Understand the strengths and weaknesses of regional polices, and how different stakeholders respond to these policies.
4. Under how supply chain and logistics management are practiced in PRD and in China in general.
courses.course_syllabus:
• Introduction - logistics process and supply chain, review of key concepts with an international perspective
• Air and sea cargo in Asia and Hong Kong
• HK's logistics infrastructure
• Agents and the shipping process
• PRD and HK – regional logistics issues
• Mainland China – regional logistics issues
• IT in SC and L management
• Emerging trends in supply chain and logistics
courses.feedback_evaluation: CTE by end of the term
courses.required_readings: Class notes will remain the most vital source of information. We are all encouraged to utilize the library for further reference material. Homework assignments, both reading and written, are extremely important to the understanding of materials presented in lectures.

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Aviation Economics
courses.description:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the economic principles shaping the global air transport industry, covering both airline and airport economics. Students will explore the structure and dynamics of air transport markets, including airline competition, airport management, and regulatory frameworks.

Key topics include the economic analysis of airline pricing and revenue management, cost structures, demand analysis, and network economics. The course examines the impact of regulatory changes, such as liberalisation, open skies agreements, airline alliances, and mergers, on industry performance and competitiveness. The evolving role of low-cost carriers and sustainability challenges in aviation will also be discussed.

The economics of airports will cover topics including airport pricing models, revenue streams, slot allocation, capacity management, and the economic relationship between airports and airlines. The role of privatisation, public policy, and investment in airport infrastructure will be analysed, along with the economic impact of airports on regional development.
Through case studies and real-world applications, students will develop analytical skills to assess strategic decisions made by airlines, airports, and regulators.

* Airline Cost Structures and Revenue Management

* Airport Economics and Management
* Aviation Policy and Regulation

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Aviation Revenue Management
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive, practice-oriented introduction to revenue management (RM) with a specific focus on the aviation industry. Through lectures, case discussions, and hands-on exercises, students learn to apply demand forecasting, assortment optimisation, dynamic pricing, seat inventory control (including overbooking), and network-level decisions to maximise profitability for airlines and airports. Emphasis is placed on data-driven decision-making, integrating RM tools with marketing and distribution channels, and understanding ethical and regulatory considerations across markets. By synthesising best practices from legacy carriers and low-cost models, students develop quantitative skills and a strategic mindset to design, evaluate, and implement RM strategies in real-world aviation settings.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Aviation Management
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of the course, students will be able to:

1. Explain core principles of revenue management and articulate their significance in aviation contexts.
2. Apply demand forecasting methods (including treatment of seasonality and shocks) to airline and airport demand.
3. Configure and evaluate assortment and fare structures (e.g., fare families, ancillary bundles) to balance customer choice and profitability.
4. Design and assess inventory control and overbooking policies (e.g., Littlewood’s Rule, EMSR) under uncertainty and legal constraints.
5. Develop pricing and competitive strategies, including dynamic pricing and ancillary revenue management.
6. Analyze network and route decisions, considering slot and capacity constraints and their implications for RM.
7. Integrate RM models and systems with marketing and distribution channels to drive commercial performance.
8. Evaluate ethical and regulatory considerations in pricing and RM practices across different jurisdictions.
9. Synthesize findings and recommendations in written and oral forms for managerial audiences.
courses.course_syllabus:
Introduction to Revenue Management in Aviation

* History and evolution of airline RM; price discrimination, dynamic pricing, forecasting fundamentals
* Aviation-specific constraints: fixed seat capacity, perishability, airport slots, schedule coordination

Demand Forecasting

* Consumer choice models and airline demand drivers
* Data sources, collection, and cleaning; seasonality, trends, and external shocks (e.g., pandemics, macro cycles)
* Forecast accuracy metrics and implications for RM

Assortment Optimization

* Fare families, classes of service, ancillaries (baggage, seats, lounge, priority)
* Optimizing product mix under operational and commercial constraints
* Customer choice, cannibalization, and profitability trade-offs

Inventory Control and Overbooking

* No-shows, cancellations, and compensation regimes
* Littlewood’s Rule, EMSR variants, nesting and protection levels
* Legal/ethical considerations and customer experience impacts

Pricing and Fare Structures

* Tariff design, fencing, and product differentiation
* Competitive pricing in O&D markets; reactions to rivals
* Dynamic pricing engines; ancillary pricing and bundling

Network and Route Management

* Schedule design and route optimization; fleet and capacity alignment
* Slot constraints and airport capacity; implications for RM controls
* Alliances, codeshare, and connectivity effects on demand and pricing

Revenue Optimization Tools and Techniques

* Dynamic programming and optimization formulations
* RM systems architecture; integration with CRS/GDS/NDC and digital channels
* Linking RM with marketing, distribution, and loyalty

Case Studies in Aviation RM

* Analysis of successful and failed RM initiatives in airlines/airports
* Industry guest insights (subject to availability)

Capstone Project and Presentations

* Group or individual projects applying RM tools to solve real or simulated aviation challenges
* Student presentations and peer reviews

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Low Altitude Operations Analytics
courses.description:
This course provides a comprehensive exploration of modern operational analytical tools for low altitude economy, through a blend of classical theory, data-driven approaches, and emerging technologies. It broadly covers topics on inventory management, risk management, network design, logistics management, capacity management, project management, and smart city operations, emphasizing novel or potential applications arising from low altitude economy.

Building on this, students examine how data analytics, deployed in Python, can enhance decision-making, enabling more responsive and accurate management strategies for operations in low altitude economy. Students will synthesize their learning through a group project on data-driven, intelligent-powered low altitude operations and a final exam, demonstrating their ability to apply analytical tools and strategic thinking to complex operational challenges.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Aviation Management
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students are expected to:

1. Apply classical and data-driven inventory models to optimize operations in low altitude economy.
2. Evaluate and manage operations risks using strategies such as risk pooling, supply diversification, and postponement.
3. Design and integrate logistics and network systems, including facility location, vehicle routing, and collaborative delivery, with a focus on drone-enabled operations.
4. Optimize resource and capacity management through flexible processes, product substitution, and modular technologies tailored to low altitude applications.
5. Develop intelligent, data-powered solutions for low altitude service and operations.
courses.course_syllabus:
* Inventory Management: classic and data-driven models.
* Risk Management: risk pooling, supply uncertainty and diversification, transshipment, postponement; case “Disruption risk mitigation in supply chains”.
* Network Design: set covering, p-median, and facility location problems; case “Wildfire detection via drones”.
* Logistics Management: transportation, shortest path, travelling salesman, vehicle routing problems; case “Charging station maintenance with batter replacement”.
* Integrated Network Design: collaborative vehicle routing, location-inventory, inventory-routing, location and/or routing problems; case “Delivering medical supplies to remote areas via drones in Rwanda”.
* Capacity Management: resource allocation, process flexibility, product substitution; case “Vehicles with interchangeable modules”.
* Project Management: bottleneck, scheduling, cash flow; case “Network expansion for delivery system”.
* Smart City Operations: intelligent transportation system, emergency service system, crowdsourced delivery.

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Low Altitude Economics
courses.description:
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the economic principles shaping the emerging low altitude economy (LAE), covering both urban air mobility operations and supporting infrastructure economics. Students will explore the structure and dynamics of LAE markets, including drone and eVTOL competition, vertiport management, and regulatory frameworks tailored to urban airspace.

Key topics include the economic analysis of LAE pricing and revenue strategies, cost structures for autonomous fleets, demand modeling for urban applications, and network economics in dense city environments. The course examines the impact of regulatory innovations, such as sandbox testing regimes, beyond-visual-line-of-sight approvals, U-space harmonization, and public-private partnerships, on market performance and scalability. The evolving role of advanced technologies like AI-driven traffic management and sustainability challenges in urban air operations will also be discussed.

The economics of LAE infrastructure will cover topics including vertiport pricing models, revenue streams from charging and data services, slot allocation in constrained airspace, capacity management for high-density operations, and the economic relationship between operators and urban stakeholders. The role of investment incentives, public policy, and funding in LAE infrastructure development will be analyzed, along with the economic impact of LAE on regional urban development in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area.

Through case studies and real-world applications, students will develop analytical skills to assess strategic decisions made by LAE operators, infrastructure providers, and regulators.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Aviation Management
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students are expected to:

1. Understand demand and supply dynamics in urban air mobility using basic economic models and stakeholder analysis, with a focus on Hong Kong/Greater Bay Area trends.
2. Estimate market sizes and evaluate investment decisions through simple cost-benefit analysis and market simulations.
3. Explore pricing strategies, economic incentives, and congestion management for sustainability and public acceptance.
4. Review business frameworks, value-chain positioning, and regulatory economics, drawing on global case studies from NASA, McKinsey, and AiRMOUR.
5. Develop strategies for market growth, policy evaluation, and stakeholder engagement via scenario discussions and team projects.
courses.course_syllabus:
This course introduces the low altitude economy (LAE), encompassing drones and urban air mobility solutions like flying taxis. We begin with the fundamentals, covering its general scope in lower airspace, various use cases such as cargo, passenger, and emergency services, relevant policies in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area (GBA), key stakeholders including regulators, operators, and communities, and enabling technologies like eVTOLs, drones, and air traffic systems.

From there, we explore practical financial tools for investment evaluation, customer behavior, and market entry strategies in HK/GBA. The course then delves into demand aspects for different applications, touching on user potential, pricing considerations, alternatives, segmentation, sensitivities, scenarios, and acceptance issues.

On the supply side, we will address infrastructure economics for facilities like vertiports and chargers, returns on investment, workforce and automation topics, network planning, competition, and operational benefits, with a midterm to reinforce concepts.

In later sessions, we examine market potential and challenges in HK/GBA, including various barriers and uncertainty management. Discussions cover external impacts like noise and environmental concerns, along with service prioritization. Students will learn about economic approaches to congestion management and regulatory frameworks for testing and integration.

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Research Methods in Microeconomics
courses.description:
This course is a combination of two separate mini-courses.

In the first half of the course we take a microeconomic perspective to analyze a number of important resource-allocating systems that are widely used in real life, including auctions, matching mechanisms, and trading platforms for financial assets. For each system we study its objective, structure, and actual performance. We will focus on the theoretical aspects of these systems, but will also examine empirical findings on how well they function.

The second half of course surveys modern methods of applied micro-econometric research. We will begin by reviewing the Rubin Causal Model, its relationship with structural models, and the econometric definition of identification. We will then proceed to consider a number of econometric estimators, research designs, and inferential methods.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil/PhD Decision Sciences and Managerial Economics or MPhil-PhD Decisions, Operations and Technology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Applied Economics:

The goal of this mini course is to introduce the students to some important economic mechanisms, and moreover to familiarize them with the analytical tools and perspectives of studying these mechanisms. For each general topic, the instructor will give an extended overview of it, and then organize the students to present classical papers on the topic, while the instructor shall supplement the presentations by providing his own comments along the way. At the end of the class students are expected to write a survey/review in a unified framework.

Applied Econometrics:

The goal of this mini course is for students to learn a set of statistical tools and research designs that are useful in conducting high-quality empirical research on topics in Applied Microeconomics and related fields. Since most applied economic research examines questions with direct policy implications, this course will focus on methods for estimating causal effects. This course differs from many other econometrics courses in that it is oriented towards applied practitioners rather than future econometricians. It therefore emphasizes research design (relative to statistical technique) and applications (relative to theoretical proofs), though it covers some of each.

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Data Visualization and Business Intelligence
courses.description: In the increasingly competitive world, the need for timely analysis of constantly expanding data to gain business intelligence and communication of the results to the key decision makers has become a vital part of a company’s operation. In the past, business intelligence used to be in the domain of IT specialists. With the advent of self-service data visualization and business intelligence tools, such as Excel BI toolkit, now anyone with adequate training can produce their own analyses with minimal support from central IT. The aim of this course is to introduce to students the Excel BI toolkit that has become an integral part of Excel since Excel 2013. Designed to handle very large amount of data, the toolkit consists of four add-ins, namely, Power Query, Power Pivot, Power View, and Power Map. Students will learn how to use these add-ins to gain business intelligence. Students who are interested in taking this course are expected to have at least intermediate level and preferably advanced level of Excel skills.

Upon completion of this course, students should:
1) have solid understanding of Excel data model and be able to design one when necessary,
2) be able to use Power Query to find and load external data and, when necessary, to shape the data into the desired forms and formats before loading into the model,
3) be able to use DAX language and Power Pivot to perform sophisticated data analysis to get key insights into business performance,
4) be able to use Power View to design interactive reports and dashboards to summarize information into instantly digestible analytics that provide at-a-glance visibility into business performance, and
5) be able to perform geospatial analysis with Power Map.

1. Data Visualization and Business Intelligence with Excel – the traditional way
2. Data Visualization and Business Intelligence with Excel BI toolkits – the revolutionary way
3. Introduction to Excel Data Model
4. Data Analysis with Power Pivot and Power Chart
5. Building Interactive Reports and Dashboards with Power View
6. Geospatial Analysis with Power Map and 3D Maps
7. Exploring Data with Power Query

courses.course_syllabus: This course covers the fundamental theories and algorithms of stochastic dynamic programming (Markov decision processes) and reinforcement learning (RL). It aims to provide the central ideas of how they are applied to model and solve various problems in different contexts. The first part of the course will focus on MDPs. We start with finite-stage models and then discuss infinite-stage models under discounted/undiscounted return and average return criteria. In the second part, we will cover popular RL algorithms like Q-learning and temporal difference learning.

Issues relating to information technology and law, such as privacy and location surveillance, digital signature, copyright, outsourcing, anti-competition and contracts are essential to our daily life. courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Data Visualization and Business Communication
courses.description: This course covers foundational perception principles, the art of designing impactful graphs, and strategies for clear, influential presentations. The course dives into the intricacies of effective data visualization and communication. The course invites some leading companies in different industries to share the skills they value in interviews and in work. Students are supposed to make presentations during classes.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Business Analytics
courses.learning_outcomes: After completing this course, students should be able to: (1) delve into the science of data visualization and the art of clear communication; (2) acquire techniques to simplify intricate data, ensuring clear, logical presentations tailored for diverse audience; (3) engage with foundational principles that enable effective communication, fostering understanding, and stimulating actionable outcomes.
courses.course_syllabus:
Content of the course:

Foundations of Perception in Data Visualization

* How to choose an effective visual, simple text, table, heatmap, scatter plots, line graph, bars, stacked vertical bar chart, waterfall chart, horizontal bar chart, area

Designing Graphs for Clarity

* Cognitive load, clutter, proximity, similarity, enclosure, closure, connection, lack of visual order, alignment, white space, non-strategic use of contrast,
* Decluttering: step-by-step, remove chart border, remove gridlines, remove data markers, clean up axis labels, label data directly, leverage consistent color

Slide Design for Optimal Communication

* Audience attention
* Preattentive attributes: bold, color, Italics, size, position

Utilizing Model Visuals in Presentation

* Line graph, annotated line graph with forecast
* 100% stacked bars, leveraging positive and negative stacked bars, horizontal stacked bars

Data-driven Storytelling

* Beginning: setting, main character, imbalance, solution
* Middle: developing situation, giving examples, including data, discuss potential options, illustrating the benefit
* End: call to action

Making Successful Presentations at Work

* For your customers or clients
* For your boss
* For your co-workers
* For community leaders or groups

Job Hunting Tips – Leading firm in Finance

* We invite a team leader in finance to share their needs in work and provide job hunting tips for students in the related industry.

Job Hunting Tips – Leading firm in E-commerce

* We invite a team leader in one of the top e-commerce firms to share their needs in work and provide job hunting tips for students in the related industry.

Job Hunting Tips – Leading Firm in Social Media

* We invite a team leader in one of the top social-media firms to share their needs in work and provide job hunting tips for students in the related industry.

Final Project: Presenting with Precision and Influence I
Final Project: Presenting with Precision and Influence II

courses.subject: DOTE
courses.title: Strategy and Innovation Management
courses.description: The aim of this course is to provide a solid grounding to students interested in managing various aspects of the innovation process and understanding it better from a policy perspective. The course is divided into two parts. Broadly, the first two-thirds of the course focuses more on analytic and strategic frameworks for managing innovation. This segment examines patterns of technological change and their impacts, planning for technological transitions, means for capturing economic benefits from innovation, and planning of innovation projects over time. The last third of the course examines more organizational issues involved in implementing strategies. These issues include management of teams and partnerships, learning within and across projects, the manager's role in forecasting and funding, directing and stopping innovation projects, technological entrepreneurship, and barriers to innovation. Case studies, both written and video-based, are used extensively to illustrate a range of technologies and the problems associated with developing them and bringing them to market.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in EMBA (Chinese)
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students will be able to:
a. Take innovation policy from theory to practice
b. Cultivate individual’s innovative mind set from within and without
c. Conduct effective innovation management
